cvEn:
Ami Levinski, son of Shoshana and Rolf, was born on 24 Tishrei 5710 (17 October 1949) at Kibbutz Na'an.

His parents were members of Dror–HeHalutz HaTzair, the youth movement, who immigrated from Chile in 1949. Until 1951 the group trained at Kibbutz Na'an in preparation for establishing Kibbutz Kisufim in the western Negev.

Ami grew up and was educated at Kibbutz Kisufim, where he attended the kibbutz elementary school.

He was a charming child with many talents and a quick grasp of languages. Even as a toddler, when he looked at the drawer bearing his name in the kibbutz kindergarten, he began to piece together the letters one by one. At the age of four he taught himself to read and write. At home he absorbed German from his mother's family and Spanish from his father's family, and in all he spoke four languages: Hebrew, English, German and Spanish.

In 1953 his sister Naomi was born. In 1956 his parents separated, and two years later his mother and sister moved to the Regavim cooperative moshav in the western Galilee. Ami stayed with his father at Kisufim, but when he was thirteen he too moved to live with his mother and younger sister in Regavim, and he studied at the "Beit Hinukh Galil Ma'aravi" regional high school, east of Nahariya.

Ami was blessed with a large and loving extended family: two more siblings from his father's new marriage and two more from his mother's new marriage. Despite the circumstances and the geographical distance, the family kept in close and warm contact. Ami, who became the eldest brother in a large family, enjoyed love and a warm bond with each of his brothers and sisters.

On completing high school, Ami enlisted in the IDF. He served in the Nahal (Fighting Pioneer Youth) Brigade and was posted to the Nahal group at the Ein Ziwan outpost in the northern Golan Heights (today Kibbutz Ein Zivan).

After his discharge, he studied teaching at the "Sde Boker" teachers' college (also known as the "Ben-Gurion Seminary"), located near Kibbutz Sde Boker in the Negev.

On 6 October 1973, with the outbreak of the Yom Kippur War, Ami was called up to fight. He was assigned to an Artillery Corps battalion and fought in the Suez Canal sector.

During the fighting, Ami contracted an illness that caused many serious health complications. He was left with a high level of disability and was recognized as an IDF disabled veteran.

In the years that followed he lived in Jerusalem, volunteered in schools in the city, helped children in distress and taught them English.

Over time his condition deteriorated. Ami died of his illness in 2007.

Ami Levinski passed away on 2 Shevat 5767 (21 January 2007), at the age of fifty-eight. He was buried in the cemetery of the Regavim moshav. He is survived by his parents, brothers and sisters.
